item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.29: Four New Typing Adventures
item.description: Meet Cipher Chase, Wordfall Reactor, Story Sprint, and Paws & Keys Adventure. Four independent pages bring spy driving with vocabulary definitions and sound checks, an everyday-word board against a computer with optional TEKS sets and definition-only hints, paste-protected passage practice, and kitten-and-puppy trails for ages 4–9. Six interface languages, current menus, and refreshed full/Games self-host downloads make the collection ready for classroom use.

item.description: All twelve packages are refreshed with the latest whiteboard, portable MySQL Save/Open, recording recovery, and creative tool improvements. Choose the full site, drop-in modules, SplatWorks apps, or independent media tools, with matching SHA-256 checksums and updated setup guides.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.24: See Your Export Progress in VideoSplat and MediaSplat
item.description: Animated purple progress bars, percentages, elapsed time, and estimates in minutes or hours help you follow subtitle burn-in and video exports. VideoSplat measures rendering and conversion separately and fixes cancellation and repeated-export progress. All twelve self-host packages are refreshed.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.23: Generate Subtitles from Speech in VideoSplat and MediaSplat
item.description: Turn English speech into editable timed subtitles on your device. Generate after recording in VideoSplat or from an existing video in MediaSplat, then download SRT or burn captions into video. This release also includes timeline zoom, fixed editing controls, recording audio checks, and refreshed self-host downloads. The speech model downloads on first use; no media is uploaded.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.21: Burn Subtitles into Video with MediaSplat and VideoSplat
item.description: Make SRT or VTT subtitles permanently visible in exported video. MediaSplat offers a video-plus-subtitles-to-MP4 workflow; VideoSplat imports styled captions onto the timeline and lets you choose burn-in during export. Adjust font size, bottom margin, outline, background, and timing offset while keeping media on your device. All twelve v3.1.21 self-host ZIPs are rebuilt with fresh SHA-256 checksums.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.20: MediaSplat, VideoSplat, and Current Self-Host Downloads
item.description: DrawSplat v3.1.20 brings MediaSplat and VideoSplat into the current self-host release. MediaSplat inspects, converts, trims, splits, and packages media locally with a browser-based FFmpeg runtime. VideoSplat supports private browser video editing, analysis, anonymization, project recovery, and export. Markdown Studio also adds DOCX and ODT export. All DrawSplat, SplatWorks, Tools, Widgets, Games, and independent media-tool ZIPs have been rebuilt with a matching SHA-256 checksum file.

item.title: AudioSplat Recorder and Sound Editor
item.description: DrawSplat.org launches an easy to use, browser-based, Chromebook-friendly audio voice recorder and editor. Meet AudioSplat.
item.author: Miguel Guhlin

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.19: AudioSplat Multitrack Recording, Editing, Google Drive, and Standalone Download
item.description: AudioSplat is now a production DrawSplat Tool for private-by-default browser audio recording and multitrack editing. Record microphones or supported shared tab/device audio, place successive takes on new tracks, drag clips between tracks, select visible waveform ranges, split and trim, zoom long recordings, undo edits, mix with mute/solo/volume/pan, and apply classroom-friendly effects. Export MP3, WAV, and additional browser-supported formats; optionally save the finished mix to Google Drive and create a share link or preview embed code. AudioSplat works without an account for local recording and editing and now ships as its own checksummed v3.1.19 self-host ZIP.

item.title: WriteSplat Update: A Classroom Word Processor Joins SplatWorks
item.description: WriteSplat is now available as the SplatWorks writing studio for teachers and students. It runs in the browser as a private, classroom-friendly word processor with local autosave, native .writesplat JSON files, practical export formats, templates, teacher tools, and kid-friendly readability feedback. The interface now follows the purple-and-white SplatWorks look, uses icon-first controls, includes language switching, and can be downloaded as its own self-host package or as part of the SplatWorks suite.

item.title: ListSplat Update: A Kid-Friendly Database Studio for SplatWorks
item.description: ListSplat is now available as the SplatWorks database studio for classroom lists, records, forms, cards, galleries, labels, and reports. It helps students build simple databases with fields, records, CSV import/export, image fields, paste-and-upload image workflows, formulas, lookup relationships, find/replace, layout visibility controls, data-quality checks, and teacher project packets. ListSplat can be downloaded by itself or inside the SplatWorks suite package.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.16 Update: SplatWorks Suite and Modular Self-Host Downloads
item.description: DrawSplat v3.1.16 makes SplatWorks available as a browser-based office suite download with GridSplat, ShowSplat, WriteSplat, and ListSplat together in one package. Schools can still download each SplatWorks app separately, and DrawSplat Tools, Widgets, and Games now have their own drop-in module ZIPs that connect when placed in the same self-host folder. The release also refreshes checksum generation, package verification, and download-page guidance for districts and teachers who want a simpler modular setup.

item.title: DrawSplat Update: ShowSplat Adds PDF, ODP, PPTX, and Editing Workflow Polish
item.description: ShowSplat now has clearer Import and Export submenus for WebDeck HTML, Markdown, PDF, ODP, and PowerPoint/PPTX workflows. WebDeck HTML and Markdown remain the cleanest editable formats. PDF import preserves pages as full-slide images, including password-protected PDFs after a prompt, and PDF export uses the browser Save as PDF flow. PPTX and ODP import/export are available as best-effort compatibility paths for common text, image, shape, background, and grouped slide content. The editor also adds selected-text bullet toggles, font-size decrease/increase buttons, a zoom slider, last-slide delete safety, smarter WebDeck import fitting, and presenter controls that auto-hide until hover.

item.title: DrawSplat v3.1.10 Update: Squirrel Run Gets Sound, Squirrel Jokes, and a Tree Dance
item.description: Squirrel Run now feels more alive in DrawSplat Games. The game adds light movement sounds, a splat sound when the squirrel loses a life, and a sound toggle for quiet classrooms. When the squirrel gets stopped by traffic, cats, dogs, or general bad road-crossing decisions, a speech bubble pops up with a short squirrel-point-of-view remark. Reaching the tree also gets a payoff: the squirrel pauses for a quick celebratory dance before the next level begins. The self-host download, release notes, README, and bundled RSS snapshot have been refreshed for v3.1.10.

item.title: DrawSplat Update: SketchSpace VR Turns Student Drawings into Virtual Rooms
item.description: SketchSpace VR is now available from the DrawSplat Tools dropdown as a standalone classroom solution. Students can print a one-page cube-room template, draw or label six panels, photograph the finished page, and explore the result as an interactive virtual room in the browser. The tool includes privacy-friendly local image handling, crop preview, trim controls, fullscreen viewing, split-view, phone viewer mode, and a language picker. To help students get started, SketchSpace VR also includes six curriculum starter layouts: citizenship, ecosystems and adaptations, geography, history, life cycles, and weather and water cycle. A separate teacher guide provides setup notes, lesson ideas, examples, assessment prompts, sharing guidance, image prompt patterns, and links to "Wallpaper Your 3D Virtual Reality Room" and "Virtual Reality with Panoform Is Easy, Engaging, and Fun for Everyone," the posts that inspired this paper-first virtual reality workflow.

item.title: DrawSplat Hub Update: A Protected Admin Space for Classroom, Campus, and District Instances
item.description: DrawSplat Hub now has a clearer public front door and a protected admin path for managing classroom, campus, and district instances. The Hub splash page stays open so people can see what the model looks like, while the live Instances Admin dashboard sits behind Google OAuth for approved administrators. The approved admin accounts are drawsplat@gmail.com and jeguhlin@gmail.com. From the Instances Admin page, a Hub admin can add an independent classroom teacher or place a teacher under a campus. The starter Apps Script registry can create a teacher folder and config file in Google Drive, then share both with the teacher as editor. That keeps setup practical while respecting Google Drive ownership rules. The self-host bundle still includes only the generic Hub and hubcampus demo, so future real campus data stays out of public downloads.

item.title: ControlAltAchieve 💡 #171
item.description: DrawSplat - Resource link I am constantly blown away by the quality of free resources being created with vibe coding. Recently my friend Miguel Guhlin shared with me his latest creation … DrawSplat. He wanted to create an interactive tool for student creativity, drawing some inspiration from programs such as Jamboard, KidPix, and others. His creation, DrawSplat, is a completely free interactive whiteboard tool for K-16 educators and students. It runs in your browser and includes a dizzying array of features including pens, paint, shapes, lines, text, notes, images, diagrams, backgrounds, stickers, graphs, widgets, and so much more. And Miguel seems to add new features everytime I check the site. Head on over to https://drawsplat.org/ to learn more and try it yourself.
